solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Two creatures, one of the two on the field?

definitions.text: one of the two on the field?

parts.note: the first creature: a chirping insect
the second creature: a flying mammal

explanation.surface: A riddle about a pair of animals, one of which is out on a playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two' tells you to find a pair of creatures. In cricket two batsmen are on the field at once, each holding one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: During a cricket innings there are always two batsmen in the middle, so two bats are on the field.

clue.text: Muscle deterioration going over a peak

parts.note: rot is decay or deterioration
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill or peak

explanation.surface: Wasting of a muscle is described as passing over a summit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'going over' means sitting above, so the first piece is placed on top of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is an anatomical term for a muscle that turns a limb, as in the rotator cuff.

clue.text: First of communications fit for message

indicators.note: asks for only the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: opening letter of communications
fit in the sense of capable

explanation.surface: Choosing the best opening for a communication.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable is a telegram, an old word for a message sent by wire.

clue.text: Paint nuts on muesli

indicators.note: nuts as an adjective means crazy, so the following letters go wild

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A breakfast instruction: add nuts to your cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like an ingredient on the cereal but signals the shuffle; 'on' is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsion is a common water-based wall paint, especially in British usage.

clue.text: Move to impound first of imports, bootleggers revealing gear?

indicators.note: impounding locks something up, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly

indicators.note: asks for only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: opening letter of imports
bootleggers smuggle illicit goods

explanation.surface: Customs officers move to seize contraband and bootleggers are exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: BUDGIE SMUGGLERS is Australian slang for tight, brief men's swimming trunks; the question mark flags the jokey definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang term names skimpy swimwear, which reveals a lot, hence revealing gear.

clue.text: Denunciation, one having cut business

indicators.note: something that has cut into another sits inside it

parts.note: trade is commerce or business
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone sacked from a firm launches an angry denunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech of criticism, a synonym for denunciation.

clue.text: Prolific toper

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests a champion drinker; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush describes abundant vegetation, and as a noun it is slang for a drunkard, which is what a toper is.

clue.text: One dragging feet in treacle, unfortunately, about sacred mantra

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters wrap around what follows
something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
om is the sacred syllable chanted in Hindu and Buddhist practice

explanation.surface: Someone wading through treacle, struggling, while chanting a mantra.
explanation.definitionFit: A latecomer arrives after the time, as someone who dawdles or drags their feet would.

clue.text: US politician atones for beating up Republican

indicators.note: something marked for beating up is due to be knocked about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: An American politician makes amends for assaulting a member of the other party.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of the US Senate, so an American politician.

clue.text: Remnant in time held in reserve

indicators.note: something held in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a sub is a substitute or reserve player
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something left over and kept back for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub is the short piece left over, as of a cigarette or pencil, so a remnant.

clue.text: See where tundra ends after melting

indicators.note: melting changes form, so these letters lose their shape and reform

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Look at the point where the frozen tundra stops once it thaws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like an instruction to look, but it is the definition in its sense of grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: To see a point is to grasp or comprehend it, as in 'I see what you mean'.

clue.text: Place importance on second lock

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: Emphasising the value of a backup lock.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress something is to emphasise it, giving it weight or priority.

clue.text: Show it with dance I created

indicators.note: something created is newly made, so the letters are formed into something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choreographer offers to demonstrate a routine they made up.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate is to point out or show something.

clue.text: Dignified exclamation of surprise

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a cry of astonishment

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a polite gasp; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Gracious means courteous and refined, and on its own it is an old-fashioned cry of surprise.

clue.text: Hybrid kiln destroyed chemical bond

parts.note: a cross is a hybrid of two breeds

indicators.note: a destroyed thing is broken apart, so its letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A combination kiln blew up, breaking a chemical bond.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-link is a bond joining one polymer chain to another in chemistry.

clue.text: Ultimately, evangelism biblical vessel for gospeller

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: final letter of evangelism
Noah's Ark is the boat in Genesis

explanation.surface: A sermon on preaching and Noah's boat, fit for an evangelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark is one of the four evangelists who wrote a Gospel, so a gospeller.

clue.text: Little work to repeat that's difficult

indicators.note: difficult suggests awkward or troublesome, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small task that is hard to do again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' belongs to the letters as well as reading as a link; all of 'to repeat' is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short light opera, literally a little opus or work.

clue.text: A short jumper, some style!

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
a frog is an animal that jumps

explanation.surface: A cry of admiration at a short sweater's style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests a British sweater, but here it is an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, bushy hairstyle, so a particular style of hair.

clue.text: Take noticeable steps with fluid measure?

parts.note: fl. is the abbreviation for fluid, as in fl oz
an ounce is a unit of measure

explanation.surface: Taking dramatic action involving a fluid ounce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluid measure' reads as one phrase, a fluid ounce, which is exactly what the pieces spell.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounce is to walk off with exaggerated, showy movements, so the steps are noticeable.

clue.text: Particular blow when part of shoe damaged

parts.note: the upper is the top part of a shoe
cut as a past participle, meaning wounded or damaged

explanation.surface: A shoe gets damaged in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damaged' looks like an anagram signal but simply gives a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is a specific punch thrown upwards in boxing, so a particular blow.

clue.text: Tense when winning, very close

parts.note: a team that is up is ahead
a tight contest is very close

explanation.surface: Nerves when ahead in a very close match.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight means anxious and on edge, a synonym for tense.

clue.text: Straight mould ruined, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: asks the solver to judge what the phrase is like when spoken

parts.note: a die is a mould and wrecked means ruined

explanation.surface: Checking whether a mould has been spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Direct means going straight, without deviation.

clue.text: Ultra-hot reprimand?

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one, it suggests a scorching telling-off; the two are separate meanings, the adjective and the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A roasting day is extremely hot, and to get a roasting is to be harshly criticised.

clue.text: Distant, due to me reminiscing, looking back somewhat

indicators.note: looking back means facing the other way, so the run of letters is read backwards
somewhat means only a part, so the letters sit inside a longer run

parts.note: the run spans due, to, me and reminiscing

explanation.surface: Someone seems distant because the speaker keeps dwelling on the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote means far away, whether in place or in manner, so distant.

clue.text: Inspector in uniform, or sergeant

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the run spans the end of uniform, or, and the start of sergeant

explanation.surface: A police rank list: an inspector in uniform, or a sergeant.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels and the British TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse is the famous fictional police inspector, so the title stands for him.

clue.text: Old footballer in team quit

parts.note: a player who is in the team is inside it
left is a past tense of leave, meaning quit

explanation.surface: A veteran player walks out of the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside left was a forward position in the old football formations, now rarely named.
explanation.definitionFit: An inside left was an attacking player in the traditional five-forward line of football.

clue.text: Fit fashion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an outburst of anger

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit fashion' reads as clothes that suit; each word is its own meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A rage is a fit of fury, and 'all the rage' means the current fashion or craze.

clue.text: Bottle — or part of one?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: nerve or cheek, British slang
second meaning: the narrow top section of a bottle

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang bottle means courage and neck means cheek or nerve; 'one' then points back to a literal bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Neck is slang for audacity, like bottle, and it is also the slim upper portion of a bottle.

clue.text: New statements — those new and old?

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are put together differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fresh declarations, set against the new and the old.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the Bible's two parts, the Old and New Testaments.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian Bible is divided into the Old and New Testaments, so these are the ones new and old.
